correctness.rationale: For full-support \(P_{X,Y}\), the published single-letter formula reduces \(R^*(g_{\mathcal A})\) to the conditional entropy of the output-tuple equivalence class of \(X\). The three non-discrete singleton columns have entropy \(h(1/3)=\log_2 3-2/3\), while column \(d\) is discrete; any block of at least two distinct \(Y\)-symbols is discrete. These facts give the six exact slope expressions in RESULT.md. The unique maximum is \(-2/3\) at merge \(\{b,c\}\). Direct entropy expansion gives \(H(\mathcal P)-H(\mathcal Q)=(5\log_2 5-8)/15>0\), and direct rate subtraction gives \(R^*(g_{\mathcal P})-R^*(g_{\mathcal Q})=2/45>0\). The minimality proofs for \(|\mathcal Y|\le3\) and \(|\mathcal X|\le2\) use monotonicity under coarsening and the two-source-symbol partition dichotomy.

The design paper describes the greedy output as an achievable set and gives one example where the front is attained; it does not state a general Pareto-optimality guarantee. The exact instance here has a unique first merge, a strict dominator on both coordinates, and a proved minimal alphabet-size regime. Targeted published-finding corpus and accessible-ledger searches found no directly matching claim; non-detection is not proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The example gives a minimal, exact witness that a polynomial greedy coarsening path can select a partition that is strictly worse in both design objectives, despite a unique first merge. This is relevant because the algorithm is a practical alternative to exponentially enumerating all partitions; the strict gaps and minimal alphabet-size boundary tell users when the path cannot be assumed to be the Pareto front. The claim is not a routine parameter increment and makes no unsupported assertion about a global approximation ratio.
